Container.Name: mybabynotes
Container.Overview:
Baby tracker built for exactly two parents sharing one baby's log — your data stays in one SQLite file on your server.
Three taps from pocket to logged: the entry sheet opens pre-stamped with the current time and a prediction of what you're about to log (alternating nursing sides, last bottle amount, feed-vs-diaper rhythm). Entries write locally first and sync when there's signal, so 3am logging never waits on the network.
Both of you, one log: a partner joins by invite and sees the same log live over websockets. Shift handoffs are a first-class flow — "I need to sleep, take him" becomes a request with a note, an auto-drafted plan from the baby's rhythm, and a handback summary instead of a "when did you…" conversation.
Installable PWA (Add to Home Screen), Now/History views with since-cards, totals, 7-day charts, sleep and nursing timers, and optional web-push reminders — no cloud account, no FCM, no telemetry.
First boot generates all secrets into /data/.env automatically; the first account registered claims the instance and invites the second parent. Everything (database + secrets) lives in the one /data share — back that folder up and you've backed up the app.
For access beyond your LAN (and for installing the PWA + push notifications, which need HTTPS), put a reverse proxy with websocket support in front — Nginx Proxy Manager or SWAG both work; enable websockets for the /app path.
Container.Requires: Remote access needs an HTTPS reverse proxy with websocket support (the PWA install prompt and push notifications require HTTPS).

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Host port for the web app. The container serves everything (app, API, websockets) on this one port.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: All state: the SQLite database and the auto-generated .env with this instance's secrets. Back this folder up.

Config.Name: APP_URL
Config.Description: Optional: your public https origin (e.g. https://babylog.example.com) when running behind a reverse proxy. Used in invite/reset emails and as the web-push VAPID subject (required for iOS push).

Config.Name: REVERB_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
Config.Description: Optional: comma-separated hostnames allowed to open websockets (e.g. babylog.example.com). Leave empty to allow any origin.
